newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian fund plans to sell foreign debt locally.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian fund plans to sell foreign debt locally.

text.p: A private Nigerian trust company on Friday said it planned to sell Nigeria's internationally quoted debt instruments locally for the first time, through a mutual fund listed on the Nigerian Stock Exchange.
The fund, to be launched on February 17 will have an initial value of $16 million and be invested in par bonds and promissory notes.
"We have already sold 60 percent of the total amount, mostly to local institutional investors," Godwin Obaseki, managing director of Securities Transactions and Trust Company told Reuters.
Obaseki said the project was a collaborative effort with Citibank's local unit, Nigeria International Bank, and UBA Nigeria, one of Nigeria's top three commercial banks.
"It will send a strong signal to the international investing community that Nigerians have faith in their own economy," Obaseki said.
"It will also ensure that a portion of payments being made on Nigeria's external debt are brought back into the country."
